newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China, Taiwan to allow applications for ship links.
newsitem.headline: China, Taiwan to allow applications for ship links.

text.p: Taiwan and China on Wednesday agreed to let shipping companies immediately apply to open routes between the two rival territories, breaking the ban on direct shipping links that had been in place since 1949.
Non-government negotiators from the two sides said they had reached a consensus following talks in Hong Kong.

"Following this meeting between the two civilian associations, and with our permission and approval to allow operation of the Kaohsiung to Fuzhou and Xiamen route, operators can immediately submit applications to China to start business," Lin Hsing-shan, head of the Taiwan delegation, told reporters.
The Chinese delegation leader said the deal would eventually lead to opening more ports between the two places.
"Following the expansion of cross-strait exchanges and the result of consultations on the direct link, there will be a gradual opening," Meng Guangju told reporters.
State-run Taiwan radio described the two sides as reaching a "concrete consensus" and said they signed a summary of the talks.
